newsitem.title: USA: Emery plans $55.9 mln upgrade to up capacity.
newsitem.headline: Emery plans $55.9 mln upgrade to up capacity.

text.p: Emery Worldwide said Tuesday it plans to spend $55.9 million to redesign and upgrade its Dayton, Ohio hub. The effort should increase capacity by more than 30 percent and improve operating efficiency, the company said.

"When this program is completed, we will be able to process 5.5 million pounds during our nightly operation. New freight handling systems and increased automation will also enable us to improve efficiency by 13.5 percent," said Emery President and Chief Executive David Beatson.

Emery, the global freight and logistics unit of CNF Transportation Inc, now moves more than four million pounds of freight a day through its Dayton hub, which was last upgraded in 1994 to increase capacity to about 3.9 million pounds.

The project is scheduled to begin in the Fall and be completed in July 2000. It will include a 145,000-square-foot building expansion, construction of a 70,000 square-foot truck dock, new sort systems to increase capacity by 20,000 parcels per hour, 21 roller deck systems to increase efficiency and the purchase of additional freight handling equipment.
The upgrade will mean 300 to 450 additional jobs when completed and will cut the number of steps required to process freight from 13 steps to four steps, Beatson said.
